answer: A storage-pledging protocol requires agents to host unique, non-deduplicable data sectors indexed in a global atlas. To prevent its operational score from falling to an eviction nadir, each identity must answer an audit pulse with deterministic proofs of data possession. An attacker incurs a verifiable marginal cost in dedicated drive capacity and disk I/O per persona. However, this design favors centralized storage farms and creates high wear on consumer-grade media.
